entries.claim: Forgejo login selection discards the instance port, so it can select a login for a different Forgejo instance on the same hostname and create the repository there.
entries.failure_scenario: `classified.host` is explicitly only a lowercased hostname, and `teaLoginFor` passes that host to `loginNamesHost`, whose documented URL comparison is likewise by hostname. Configure tea logins `prod-3000` for `https://forge.example:3000` and `prod-3001` for `https://forge.example:3001`, then request `--remote-url https://forge.example:3001/john/r.git`. Both records name `forge.example`; list order can select `prod-3000`. The create is then pinned with `--login prod-3000` and lands on port 3000, while the subsequent git remote is added using the requested port-3001 URL. This silently creates an unintended repository and leaves the local repository pointing at a different instance.
